page: Vultr voc-g-32c-128gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical AMD EPYC cores with multithreading enabled. The system operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 640 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance scoring 99,997.49 and PassMark CPU score reaching 63,947.14, both placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength; large-block read-only operations reach 537.96 GB/sec and write operations reach 292.8 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the top 10%. However, single-threaded tasks show more moderate performance, with gzip compression and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the middle 50%.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without noisy-neighbor interference, making it a reliable option for sustained workloads. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a balanced allocation for general-purpose computing, though workloads requiring extreme memory-to-core ratios or specialized hardware acceleration will find limitations due to the lack of a GPU and the fixed 128 GB RAM capacity.

This server configuration is suitable for multi-threaded applications, database operations, and moderate LLM text generation, as demonstrated by its strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (209.38 GB/sec) and 30.05 tokens/sec text generation speed on 7B models. It is also appropriate for Redis deployments, achieving 73.66 million SET operations per second, and general-purpose web serving.
